0.d.rationale: CC BY 4.0 is linked as a resolving IRI (machine-readable). An ODRL data use policy explicitly permits use 'including AI/ML training'; the only prohibitions shown (re-identifying, contacting, profiling) do not bar AI/ML reuse.
gaps: Expose the full ODRL prohibition list untruncated / as conditionsOfAccess so the DUA terms are reviewable alongside the license

2.d.rationale: rai:dataBiases names concrete, data-specific biases: single-host scope, author's personal infrastructure as the benign baseline, 2.8% malicious class imbalance with metric guidance, a 0.3% time-window-only mislabel rate, and Poisson attack timing that models could learn. Missingness is quantified per column with causes, and the malicious/benign (state-vs-control) balance is stated; demographic and clinical questions do not apply to server telemetry.
gaps: Quantify how the benign baseline differs from enterprise telemetry (e.g., service mix, traffic volume) rather than only asserting underrepresentation
State any temporal-coverage assumptions (no rai:dataCollectionTimeframe given)

2.e.rationale: Domain-appropriate QC is documented: nine automated label-validation checks (label consistency, regex spot checks per attack type, campaign containment, temporal monotonicity, session coherence, etc.) implemented in a linked, resolving script pinned to v0.4.2, plus independent relabelling of 2,000 events by two analysts with agreement statistics and signature-based filtering of the benign baseline.
gaps: Report QC on capture fidelity (dropped eBPF events, log rotation gaps) and publish per-check pass results, not just the claim that all streams pass

4.a.rationale: Acquisition names the sources (author-operated servers, isolated lab VM), gives a specific exemption basis for retrospective data (UM-Dearborn IRB protocol HUM-DEMO-0001, exempt under 45 CFR 46.104(d)(4), explicitly covering AI/ML training release), and confirms legitimacy (no third-party systems, no deception or coercion). A management plan is supplied via rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan with named steward and successor.
gaps: Link a standalone DMP/DMSP document (the only extracted link is the issue tracker)
Populate structured ethicalReview / irb fields and name the reviewer; the protocol ID looks like a placeholder

4.b.rationale: Sensitivity is declared (HL7 confidentiality M) and matched to a specific disclosure risk: 860,529 benign rows retain 11,413 public client IPs. A named privacy impact assessment (UM-Dearborn Information Security, March 2026) rated this low risk with reasons, host identities are scrubbed to a synthetic identity, and re-identification risk is reassessed annually and on new linkage sources with a removal-on-request path.
gaps: Link the PIA report itself rather than summarizing it
Consider hashing/truncating retained public IPs or justify why they must remain verbatim in raw_line

4.c.rationale: The data is openly released under CC BY 4.0 with an ODRL policy that states permitted uses (research, benchmarking, AI/ML training) and ethical prohibitions (re-identifying, contacting or profiling individuals), which suits retained IP addresses. No high-risk modality (voice, genome, face, geolocation) is present, so modality-specific prohibitions are not required, and a DAC contact is given.
gaps: Replace the DAC contact security-gym-dac@example.org (a reserved placeholder domain, so not demonstrably active) with a real address
Surface the full prohibition list (evidence shows it truncated)

5.b.rationale: Data is deposited in Zenodo, a recognized generalist repository with DOIs (concept and version), and mirrored on Hugging Face. No community-standard specialist repository exists for host/security log streams of this kind, so a generalist deposit meets the 2 condition.
gaps: Optionally also register in a security-data catalogue (e.g., IMPACT-style) if one becomes the community norm

5.c.rationale: The maintenance plan names a data steward and a successor steward (UM-Dearborn Library Research Data Services), gives a 20-year retention period and a 5-year update commitment through 2031, states the deprecation policy, and sends changes in law or repository policy and removal requests to the DAC within 30 days, which covers stewardship, maintenance and policy handling.
gaps: Link a formal DMP document; the extracted link is the GitHub issue tracker
Name the governance committee members and fix the placeholder DAC contact

6.b.rationale: All 6 distributions have remote https contentUrls on Zenodo and Hugging Face, both reachable and both with publicly documented REST/Hub APIs that allow scripted bulk download without authentication. The data is open, so no access procedure is needed.
gaps: Reference the API mechanism explicitly in metadata (e.g., Zenodo REST record endpoint, HF datasets repo id / load_dataset call) rather than relying on file URLs alone

6.c.rationale: Files are an open format (zstd), and the software environment is declared in machine-executable form: a pinned container image ghcr.io/j-klawson/security-gym:0.4.2 and a pinned PyPI wheel, with a 16 GB RAM hardware requirement. No proprietary or local-only compute is required.
gaps: Attach usedContainer to the 4 computations (currently 0/4) so each generation step is reproducible in the container
Add software descriptions for the three tools (currently empty)
